llama.raw_text:
Avoid growing tomato in the same field season after season
Rotate with non-host crops such as cereals and legumes
Do not follow tomato with chilli or brinjal
Stake plants and use drip irrigation to reduce leaf wetness
Collect and destroy infected leaves, shoots and fruits
Spray only need-based, label-claim pesticides
Conduct agro-ecosystem analysis weekly

llama.raw_text:
Brown spots with concentric rings in a bull's eye pattern with yellow margin on the photographed leaf.

Early blight on a tomato leaf.

Fruit gets infected through calyx or stem attachment.

Irregular leaf spots mostly appear from marginal portion of leaves.

Symptoms are V shaped and progress towards midrib.

These lesions are having prominent yellowing on their outer margin due to host specific toxin produced by the pathogen.

Mostly disease appears in vegetative phase of plant growth before flowering.

This is a common disease of tomato occurring on the foliage at any stage of the growth.

The fungus attacks the foliage causing characteristic leaf spots and blight.

Early blight is first observed on the plants as small, black lesions mostly on the older foliage.

llama.raw_text:
Water-soaked black lesions on leaves and stems

Lesions expand rapidly and the entire leaf becomes necrotic

White sporulation on leaves

Dark brown lesions on fruit

Soft rot and disintegration of fruits

Light-pale green water soaked dead area

Wet in morning and dried, shriveled in daylight

Enlarges rapidly until entire leaves are killed and exposing all the fruits for infection

Downy white fungus develops near the outer margin of lesion on underside of the leaves

Green and ripe fruit affected by the blight appear as greenish brown

Internal tissues become spongy with bad odour

Grow resistant variety/hybrid Arka Abhed F1

llama.raw_text:
Small, round to irregular spots with grey centre and dark margin on leaves.

Spots join and leaves are blighted; complete defoliation.

Stems and flowers are also affected.

Complete defoliation of affected leaves.

Stems and flowers are sometimes attacked.

Fruits are rarely attacked.

Remove affected plant parts.
